A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OMNI-EPIC. Their main text, figures, tables, prompts and extensive task-code appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original task-generation experiments, five short RL-training runs, and quantitative comparisons of diversity and open-ended progress in Sections 4–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds component ablations, human evaluation, sensitivity analyses and Ant-robot demonstrations.

M1.justification: The archive retrieval, task/environment generators, interestingness filtering, DreamerV3 transfer learning and success-checking procedure remain unchanged. Core prompts and task code match. v3 clarifies the use of code-based success detection and relocates existing VLM material to Appendix C; these do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: The R2D2/PyBullet task coverage is retained. Appendix P adds Ant-robot training with eight-dimensional continuous control and four illustrated task demonstrations, extending embodiment and control requirements beyond the original six-action R2D2 setting within the same simulator.

E2.justification: v3 retains OMNI-EPIC Learning Progress Only and OMNI-EPIC w/o archive, while adding evaluated variants using training from scratch, uniformly sampled archive examples, successful examples only, and no learning-progress prompting. Appendix G and Figure 41 substantially expand the comparison set around the system's central components.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include transfer-versus-scratch comparisons on the same generated tasks with equal two-million-step budgets, a 50-participant video-rating study, and diversity measurements at additional discretization levels. These extend the evaluation protocol; v3's clarification of pooled PCA and the original binning procedure does not establish that retained experiments changed.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's archive and interestingness controls, Appendix G tests transfer learning, example retrieval, failed-task examples and learning-progress prompting. Appendices H–I add human checks of success judgments, diversity sensitivity to discretization, and analysis of learned-task fractions over time. These substantially strengthen component and robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report three simulated-learning runs, five RL runs, medians with 95% confidence intervals, and Mann-Whitney U tests. New results extend these existing reporting practices. Neither increased replication of retained experiments nor a new statistical estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Original results, including Figure 4 and the illustrated run's 16 successes, six failures and one uninteresting task, are retained. New findings include median success of 63.2% with transfer versus 36.8% from scratch, 5/7/0 learned generated tasks in the three prompt/retrieval ablations, and 72.7% human–detector agreement. Added sensitivity results show that short-run diversity differences are not always significant. These are new comparisons and findings, not improvements over v2 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: The Darwin Completeness concept and ANNECS-OMNI criterion are retained. No new theorem, proof or formal derivation is introduced. Expanded descriptions of embeddings, PCA and binning clarify existing empirical measurement rather than introduce new mathematical theory.

C1.justification: The abstract changes 'can endlessly create' to 'has the potential to endlessly create,' and the conclusion similarly qualifies endless generation. The core contribution—code-generated, interesting and learnable curricula—remains, with more cautious claims about indefinite continuation.

C2.justification: v3 adds caveats about resemblance to foundation-model training data, cyclic task rejection and the absence of demonstrated cross-task generalization. The generalist-training discussion, moved from Section 5 to Appendix O, changes 'straightforward' feasibility into a substantial future undertaking. These refine the retained applicability discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly states that all code is open-sourced and provides a direct repository link. v3 also documents pooled PCA/binning, human-study instructions and compensation, the learning-progress ablation prompt, and Ant action bounds. Existing hyperparameter tables, hardware disclosures, core prompts and task code remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds intrinsic-motivation and procedural-generation context, including Oudeyer, Baranes, Colas, Shaker, Juliani and Justesen references. The relocated VLM discussion cites Du et al. (2023) in place of Christiano et al. (2017). Positioning relative to OMNI and environment-design approaches remains broadly unchanged; many other citation edits concern the same works.

P1.justification: There are targeted language corrections and clearer method and metric explanations. Existing VLM discussion and prompts are consolidated in Appendix C, and generalist-training discussion moves to Appendix O. The main narrative and extensive existing appendices remain largely intact, alongside bibliography and conference-header edits.

P2.justification: v3 adds substantial visual material: three ablation montages, the human-annotation interface, two sensitivity figures, a learned-task-fraction curve and Ant demonstrations. Existing plots are retained and rearranged, including v2 Figures 33–34 becoming v3 Figures 37 and 40. Main-text figures also move within the revised layout.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation of the curriculum mechanisms through controlled transfer comparisons and component ablations, tests diversity-metric robustness, and independently checks success judgments with humans. These address important evidential gaps in v2, while qualified claims improve calibration. The 72.7% human agreement still leaves success measurement imperfect, and generalist performance remains untested, but the added evidence and transparency provide a substantial overall quality gain.
